aspects.title: Announced text lacks the visual context that makes it meaningful (no offscreen text for AT)
aspects.plain: The visible text only makes sense from its on-screen position (a lone '3' beside a cart icon), and no hidden context is added, so a screen-reader user just hears an orphaned '3'.
aspects.description: The status is announced cleanly and the whole atomic string is read — so tools and seeds pass. The failure is that the VISIBLE text relies on spatial/visual proximity for meaning, and no offscreen/extra text was added to the live region to supply that context to a non-sighted user. The Understanding's canonical example: a bare '3' appears next to a shopping-cart icon — sighted users understand 'cart: 3', AT users hear an orphaned '3'. Likewise a green checkmark + 'Done' next to a specific row, or 'Saved' with no album name where the visible popup sits over the 'Wedding' album. The remediation (add offscreen 'in shopping cart' / the album name, or place the icon's alt text inside the atomic region) is exactly the human judgment the SC's 'Non-displayed text specific to AT users' section calls for, and it cannot be derived from markup.
aspects.scLimb: Non-displayed text specific to AT users — Understanding 'Non-displayed text specific to AT users' + 'Modification of status text' (add offscreen context); ARIA22 shopping-cart example.
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus; the seeds only test missing/silent live regions, never a present-and-announcing region whose announced content is contextually impoverished. Automated tools cannot judge that '3' is insufficient without 'items in cart' — the text is non-empty, the region is valid, and inferring that the VISUAL layout supplied context the AT string lacks requires reasoning about meaning and spatial relationship, not parsing the DOM.

references.doc: Understanding 4.1.3 (Non-displayed text specific to AT users)
references.quote: the addition of visible text does not by itself convey sufficient information to the user of assistive technology. For example, the proximity of new content to other pieces of information on the screen may provide a visual context that is lacking in the text alone
In this case it would also be a courtesy to add offscreen text such as "in shopping cart" to the message.

Because it adds visual context, the shopping cart image — with succinct and accurate alt text — is also placed in the container. Due to the aria-atomic value, a screen reader will announce "Shopping cart, six items".

pages.scenario: E-commerce hiking-gear store: a valid role=status/aria-live=polite/aria-atomic=true cart badge updates from 0 to 1/2/3 on Add-to-Cart, announcing only the bare number. The word 'cart' that gives the number meaning lives on the adjacent icon glyph's aria-label (so 1.1.1 passes) but sits outside the atomic region and is never re-read on update.
pages.mechanism: On update the polite live region announces its entire atomic contents — just the digit ('three'). It does not re-read the sibling glyph's 'Shopping cart' aria-label, because a polite live announcement speaks the changed region's atomic contents, not adjacent unchanged nodes. AT hears an orphaned number; remediation per the Understanding is offscreen 'in shopping cart' text or placing the cart image with alt INSIDE the atomic region (ARIA22).
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The live region is structurally perfect (role present before update, valid aria-live/aria-atomic, non-empty) and the adjacent icon has a non-empty aria-label, so name/role and F103 missing-role checks all pass. No automated rule asserts the announced text must be semantically self-sufficient; judging that '3' is meaningless without 'items in cart' requires understanding the visible cart icon supplied context the announced string omits.

citation.quote: where only the number in this string was coded as an updated chunk of content, the resulting experience for screen reader users could be to only hear "three", which may not be sufficient information to provide context for the user. In such situations, marking the entire "3 items" string as the status text would normally be a better solution. ... In this case it would also be a courtesy to add offscreen text such as "in shopping cart" to the message.

pages.scenario: SaaS CRM leads pipeline grid. Changing a row's Stage select autosaves and injects 'Saved ✓' into that row's own per-row valid live region. The whole string is announced atomically, but it names only the action — never which lead. The lead identity is conveyed only by which visual row the green checkmark lands in.
pages.mechanism: A live region announces only its own atomic contents, not its DOM ancestors; sitting inside the <tr> does not make the row's lead-name cell part of the announcement. AT hears 'Saved' with no subject; across multiple edits the announcements are indistinguishable. Fix: include offscreen row context (lead name/company) inside the per-row status.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Every per-row live region is valid, present before update, and filled atomically; the form controls have rich accessible names — so it is not an F103 missing-role case and not a naming failure. No automated rule asserts a status string must identify its subject when the subject is established only by table-row position; recognizing the gap requires reasoning about table semantics and visual grouping.

citation.quote: There may be cases where the addition of visible text does not by itself convey sufficient information to the user of assistive technology. For example, the proximity of new content to other pieces of information on the screen may provide a visual context that is lacking in the text alone.

pages.scenario: Photo-management app viewing the 'Wedding' album. Saving a photo fires a bottom-center toast (valid role=status/aria-atomic, present before action) that shows a check + 'Saved'. The destination album name is in the top bar and active sidebar item the toast visually floats over, but the announcement omits it — the verbatim Understanding 'Saved in Wedding album' case.
pages.mechanism: The polite region announces 'Saved' (check is aria-hidden) then auto-dismisses after 3.5s. A sighted user reads 'Saved' positioned over the 'Wedding' header and understands the destination; AT hears a bare 'Saved' with no album and the toast vanishes before the surrounding context can be discovered (which F103 says a status must not require). Remediation: include the album name inside the atomic region.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The toast is a present, non-empty, correctly-roled live region announced in full — not an F103 missing-role failure and not a partial-atomic clip. No automated rule asserts a status must name the object/destination of an action when that object is conveyed by the toast's placement over unchanged page chrome; detecting it needs spatial+semantic judgment no DOM scan performs.

citation.quote: After a user puts a photo in an album in an online photo app, the app dynamically displays a popup message of "Saved in 'Wedding' album", which is also read by a screen reader.

pages.scenario: Concert-ticketing seat map (rows 12–15, seats A–H). Each seat button has a complete accessible name and valid aria-pressed. Selecting a seat turns it green and writes 'Selected' into a shared valid live region — never 'Seat 14C selected'. Which seat is conveyed only by which grid cell changed color.
pages.mechanism: The seat button announces its own name on focus and 'pressed' on toggle, but the separate shared status region — meant to confirm the outcome — announces only 'Selected' and never restates the seat coordinate. Reviewing picks yields a stream of identical 'Selected' announcements. Fix: announce 'Seat 14C selected' with the coordinate inside the atomic region.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Seat buttons pass name/role/state checks and the status region is present, valid, non-empty, and announced — neither an F103 nor a 4.1.2 failure. No automated rule asserts the confirmation status must restate the acted-on control when its identity is conveyed by grid position; mapping map-position to required status text is human judgment.

citation.quote: There may be cases where the addition of visible text does not by itself convey sufficient information to the user of assistive technology. For example, the proximity of new content to other pieces of information on the screen may provide a visual context that is lacking in the text alone.

pages.scenario: RTL Arabic (dir=rtl, lang=ar) fintech stock watchlist. Each row's Change cell is its own valid live region. Refreshing prices writes the new percentage (e.g. '+2.3%') into each region, announced in full — but with no ticker symbol. Which equity moved is conveyed only by which row (the symbol in the first column) the change sits beside.
pages.mechanism: Each polite region announces only its atomic contents ('plus 2.3 percent'), not the row's symbol cell, because a live region speaks its own changed contents not adjacent unchanged cells. AT hears a stream of percentages with no tickers exactly when timing is critical. RTL does not help: announcement order follows the accessibility tree and the symbol is simply absent from the region. Fix: include the symbol inside each atomic region.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Every Change cell is a present, valid, non-empty live region announced in full, and dir/lang are correct so i18n linting passes too — not an F103 or partial-atomic case. No automated rule asserts a numeric status must carry the identity of the entity it describes when that identity is set by row position; inferring '+2.3%' is meaningless without the symbol requires understanding the table's row semantics.

citation.quote: Check that the web page does not fail WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.3 Status

pages.scenario: SaaS pricing page with three plan columns (Starter/Team/Business). A team-size select recomputes the best plan, moves a green 'Best value' ribbon to the winning column, and updates a shared valid live region — to just 'Best value'. Which plan won is conveyed only by which column heading the ribbon visually sits over; the ribbon itself is aria-hidden.
pages.mechanism: On recompute the polite region announces 'Best value' with no plan name; the ribbon is aria-hidden and a live region does not read the column heading it aligns with. Changing team size yields repeated context-free 'Best value' announcements. Fix: announce the plan name inside the atomic region (e.g. 'Best value: Business plan').
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The live region is present before update, valid, non-empty, and announced in full; each column has a real <h2> heading; making the decorative ribbon aria-hidden is legitimate — so no F103, empty-region, or heading failure. No automated rule states a recommendation status must name which item it recommends when identity is conveyed by the column heading the recommendation sits over; recognizing the aria-hidden ribbon removed the last programmatic link requires reasoning about visual column structure.

citation.quote: Such additional context can be critical where the status message text alone will not provide an equivalent to the visual experience.

aspects.title: Removal/absence of status text conveys meaning, but nothing is announced when it disappears
aspects.plain: A 'Loading…' message is announced when it appears, but its disappearance (which signals 'done' to sighted users) is silent, so a screen-reader user never learns it finished.
aspects.description: A 'Loading…' / 'Busy' / 'Processing payment…' message is correctly placed in a live region and IS announced when it appears — so it passes the appearance-only test. The failure is on the OTHER edge: for sighted users the DISAPPEARANCE of that message signals 'now done / available', but for AT users the silent removal conveys nothing, and no replacement 'system available' / 'results ready' message is announced. The SC explicitly flags that absence can itself be status. Detecting this requires reasoning that the END of the waiting state is itself information the user needs — a temporal/semantic inference, not a markup check; tools never even observe the removal, let alone judge that it carried meaning.
aspects.scLimb: Removal of status text — Understanding 'Removal of status text' (absence itself conveys status; needs a non-visible 'system available' message).
aspects.whyUncovered: No ACT case; the seeds model only the additive direction ('message appears but isn't announced'). The removal-conveys-status case is entirely absent. Automated tools cannot catch it: removing a node from a polite region produces no announcement by design, the DOM after removal is clean, and inferring that 'busy text vanished, therefore the author owed a non-visible system-available message' demands understanding the workflow's meaning over time.

references.quote: In situations where status text is entirely removed, its absence may itself convey information about the status. The most obvious example of this is where a message is displayed that the system is "busy" or "waiting". For a sighted user, when this text disappears, it is normally an indication that the state is now available.

non-sighted users would be unaware of this change, unless the end of the waiting state results in a change of context for the user. Where updating the visible message (e.g., to "system available") is not feasible, the use of a non-visible status message, such as "system available", ensures equivalent status information is provided.

pages.scenario: Auto-parts AJAX 'Parts finder': a 'Searching the catalog…' spinner is announced in a role=status polite live region on entry, then the region is emptied on completion and the result rows plus an '8 matches found' count are injected into a separate non-live <section>. The disappearing spinner is the only 'done' cue; AT hears neither the end of the wait nor the count.
pages.mechanism: Phase-1 busy text enters a valid role=status/aria-live=polite region (announced). Phase-2 sets status.textContent='' — clearing a polite region produces no announcement, so the end of the waiting state is silent. The 'N matches found' count (itself a status message per the SC's search examples) is placed in #results which has role=null/aria-live=null, so it is never announced either.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: At every snapshot the markup is valid (real live region, labeled search input, well-formed result rows). axe/WAVE/Lighthouse never press Search, never observe the live region being EMPTIED on completion, and have no model that 'the busy text disappeared, therefore a done/count status was owed.' Inferring that the absence of the spinner is itself status, and that the count should have been announced, is a temporal/semantic workflow judgment, not a markup rule.

The most obvious example of this is where a message is displayed that the system is "busy" or "waiting". pages.scenario: LMS reflective-essay editor (contenteditable) autosaves. A 'Saving your changes…' pill is announced in a top-bar role=status polite region on entry, then on success the pill is simply removed and the save-status area goes blank — no 'All changes saved' replacement. Sighted users infer success from the pill vanishing; AT users hear 'Saving…' then permanent silence and cannot tell if the draft saved before the deadline.
pages.mechanism: finishSave() runs saveStatus.textContent='' on the polite region. Emptying a live region announces nothing, so the save's success — encoded purely as the REMOVAL of the busy pill (a visual-only cue) — is never spoken. The intended 'All changes saved' status ('success of an action') is never authored because the saved state was represented as the absence of the pill.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The DOM is always well-formed (valid live region, labeled editable textbox, toolbar). axe/WAVE/Lighthouse do not type into the editor, do not wait out the debounce, and do not observe that the region is emptied rather than updated on success. No static rule can infer that the cleared pill represented 'saved' and therefore owed an announcement — recognizing that the absence of the busy text carries the success status is a semantic, time-dependent inference.

pages.scenario: PASS boundary control. Government 2FA identity step: 'Sending verification code…' is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then the SAME region is overwritten in-place with '✓ Code sent to the mobile number ending 47. Enter it below.' (announced), and the OTP input is revealed. The end of the wait is announced by REPLACING the busy text, not by silently removing it — the correct 'Removal of status text' remediation.
pages.mechanism: The polite region is updated in place (innerHTML set to a fresh completion message), never emptied. A new text mutation inside a polite region is announced, so AT hears both the start AND the explicit end ('Code sent…') of the waiting state. The busy text's disappearance is no longer the only 'done' signal — the replacement string is the 'system available'-equivalent the SC calls for. Same component family as case-01/02 but the opposite outcome (replace vs. empty).
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Tools cannot confirm this PASSES any more than they can confirm the failures: at a static snapshot they see only a valid live region and a labeled input. They never trigger the action, never observe that the busy message is REPLACED rather than CLEARED, and cannot judge that the replacement string conveys the equivalent 'done' status. The pass/fail distinction turns entirely on a runtime, semantic comparison (was the end-of-wait announced?) that no scanner performs — which is why a correct page is indistinguishable from the failing ones to a tool.

citation.quote: In situations where status text is entirely removed, its absence may itself convey information about the status. … Where updating the visible message (e.g., to "system available") is not feasible, the use of a non-visible status message, such as "system available", ensures equivalent status information is provided.

pages.scenario: Candle-shop checkout: 'Processing payment…' plus an indeterminate progress bar is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on success the busy region is emptied AND a brand-new confirmation panel ('Thank you — your order is confirmed', Order #LUM-50418) is revealed as an ordinary <div> with no role=status/aria-live. AT hears 'Processing payment…' then silence — neither the end of the wait nor whether the card was charged, risking a duplicate charge if they re-press.
pages.mechanism: Double failure: (1) proc.textContent='' empties the busy live region (silent end-of-wait); (2) the confirmation result is rendered in #confirm, a plain div with role=null/aria-live=null, so revealing it via display triggers no announcement. The success/result-of-an-action status ('order is confirmed', order number) is conveyed visually only, and the vanished progress bar is the only 'done' cue.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Across snapshots the markup is valid: a live region exists, the form is labeled, and the confirmation panel is well-formed HTML with good contrast. axe/WAVE/Lighthouse do not click Pay, never see the busy region emptied, and treat a div of confirmation text as ordinary content — they cannot infer it is a status message that needed announcing, nor that the vanished progress bar was the only 'done' signal. Recognizing that both the removal and the out-of-region result leave the AT user unable to know whether payment succeeded is a contextual, temporal judgment about a money-moving workflow.

However non-sighted users would be unaware of this change, unless the end of the waiting state results in a change of context for the user.

pages.scenario: Bilingual pharmacy refill: 'Checking insurance coverage…' plus a spinner is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on completion the busy region is emptied and a plain #priceOut block ('Your copay: $12.00 · Covered by BlueShield Select PPO · 88% paid') is revealed with no role=status/aria-live. The copay outcome is itself a status message yet is conveyed visually only, and the end of the wait is silent — a decision-blocking gap on a health-and-cost page.
pages.mechanism: cov.textContent='' empties the busy live region (no announcement on removal), and #priceOut is shown via display (role=null/aria-live=null — never announced). The coverage outcome reports the success/result of the check (analogous to '5 results returned' / 'form successfully submitted') so it qualifies as a status message, but it carries no status semantics; combined with the silent removal, an AT user learns neither that the check finished, whether the drug is covered, nor the cost.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The page is valid at every snapshot: a real live region, a labeled button, correctly used lang=es spans, and a well-formed price block with good contrast. axe/WAVE/Lighthouse never click Check, never see the live region emptied, and read the copay figure as ordinary body copy — they cannot judge that a coverage outcome is a status message owed an announcement, nor that the vanished spinner was the only 'done' cue. Determining that the silent removal plus silent result blocks a coverage/cost decision is a contextual, temporal inference no static rule encodes.

citation.quote: In situations where status text is entirely removed, its absence may itself convey information about the status. The most obvious example of this is where a message is displayed that the system is "busy" or "waiting". For a sighted user, when this text disappears, it is normally an indication that the state is now available. However non-sighted users would be unaware of this change …

pages.scenario: Restaurant reservation widget: 'Checking availability…' plus a spinner is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on success the busy region is emptied and a previously-disabled 'Reserve this table' button is enabled (its label unchanged). Sighted users read the spinner vanishing + the greyed button lighting up as 'a table is available'; AT users hear 'Checking availability…' then silence, with no 'Available — you can book' status and only a bare disabled→enabled control flip.
pages.mechanism: avail.textContent='' empties the busy live region (silent end-of-wait). The availability outcome is conveyed only by #book flipping disabled→enabled with an UNCHANGED accessible name ('Reserve this table'); a screen reader does not spontaneously announce a state change on an unfocused control. The SC's excepted-examples note says control state changes are handled by 4.1.2 and do NOT discharge the obligation to announce the availability STATUS that the removed busy text represented — so neither path fires.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: At every snapshot the markup is valid: a real live region, labeled selects, and a native <button disabled> (toggling disabled is legitimate). axe/WAVE/Lighthouse never press Check, never observe the live region being emptied, and see a button-enable as a normal disabled toggle — not as a missing status announcement. They cannot judge that the availability outcome was a status message owed a 'now available' string, nor that the vanished spinner was the only 'done' cue. That is a temporal, workflow-meaning inference, not a markup check.

citation.quote: In situations where status text is entirely removed, its absence may itself convey information about the status. The most obvious example of this is where a message is displayed that the system is "busy" or "waiting". For a sighted user, when this text disappears, it is normally an indication that the state is now available. However non-sighted users would be unaware of this change, unless the end of the waiting state results in a change of context for the user. Where updating the visible message (e.g., to "system available") is not feasible, the use of a non-visible status message, such as "system available", ensures equivalent status information is provided.

aspects.title: Non-textual status (icon/sound) given a status role but no usable text alternative
aspects.plain: A status shown only by an icon or chime is placed in a live region but has no text alternative, so the region fires yet the screen reader announces nothing meaningful.
aspects.description: A status is conveyed purely by a non-text change — a spinner->checkmark icon swap, a red 'x' badge, a color/shape change, or an audio chime — and the author DID wrap it in a live region (role=status/alert), so the absence-of-role checkers and the seeds pass. The failure is that the icon carries empty/decorative/absent alt (alt='', aria-hidden, a CSS background image with no text, an SVG with no accessible name) or the sound has no visual+text equivalent, so the live region fires but announces nothing, or announces a filename, or announces a meaningless symbol. The SC routes this through 1.1.1: the role surfaces the change, but only a correct text alternative makes the change intelligible. Deciding that the icon IS a status indicator (not decoration) and that its alt misrepresents/omits the state is a semantic + visual judgment a checker cannot make — the markup is valid and a missing-alt linter cannot tell that this particular swap conveys status.
aspects.scLimb: Non-textual status content — Understanding 'Non-textual status content' (icon/sound surfaced via 1.1.1 text alternative + a status role).
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus; the seeds model only missing/silent live regions on textual messages, never a present live region whose status is carried by a non-text change with a missing/empty/wrong text alternative. Automated alt-text checkers cannot tell that a specific icon swap conveys status (vs. decoration), and a present role=status region with an alt='' icon is structurally valid; recognizing the state change is meaningful and the alternative fails to convey it requires visual + semantic reasoning.

references.quote: Where an icon or sound indicates a status message, this information will be surfaced by the screen reader through a combination of two things: 1) existing WCAG requirements governing text alternatives (under Success Criterion 1.1.1 Non-Text Content), and 2) the requirement of this current success criterion to supply an appropriate role.
Because it adds visual context, the shopping cart image — with succinct and accurate alt text — is also placed in the container.
After a user activates a process, an icon symbolizing 'busy' appears on the screen. The screen reader announces "application busy".

pages.scenario: Insurance auto-quote wizard (step 2 of 5). Inline licence-number validation swaps a neutral gray dot to a red 'X' SVG inside a present role="alert" region on invalid submit. The alert fires but its only child is an aria-hidden SVG with no text, so it announces an empty string.
pages.mechanism: role="alert" container is present at load and its mutation fires the live-region boundary, but the injected red-X SVG carries aria-hidden="true" with no <title>/aria-label and there is no sibling text node, so the region's computed text content is the empty string — the screen reader announces 'alert' then silence while a sighted user sees an unmistakable error X. Headless check confirmed announced text == "" with the red-X path present.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The live region is valid and pre-placed (F103/live-region seeds pass), and aria-hidden="true" is the RECOMMENDED markup for a decorative SVG, so no missing-alt/empty-name rule fires (there is no missing attribute to catch). Deciding that this specific dot->X swap conveys the error status (vs. ornament) and therefore needed a text alternative, and that the alert announces nothing, is a visual + semantic judgment no axe/WAVE/Lighthouse rule performs.

citation.quote: Changes in content are not restricted to text changes. Where an icon or sound indicates a status message, this information will be surfaced by the screen reader through a combination of two things: 1) existing WCAG requirements governing text alternatives (under Success Criterion 1.1.1 Non-Text Content), and 2) the requirement of this current success criterion to supply an appropriate role.

pages.scenario: LMS assignment-upload widget (Cell Biology 210). A spinner is injected into a present role="status" region on submit (busy), then swapped for a green-check on completion (done). The image swap is the only busy/success indicator.
pages.mechanism: role="status" (implicit aria-live=polite, aria-atomic=true) re-announces its contents on change, but its sole descendant is an , which contributes no text — so the region announces "" while uploading AND at success. The blind student hears total silence at the exact moment the assignment submits. Headless check confirmed announced text == "" with img alt == "".
pages.selectorNote: Resting empty role=status; spinner/check img (alt="") injected on submit
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: role="status" is present at load (live-region seeds pass), and alt="" is the W3C-recommended value for a decorative image, so the 'images must have alternate text' rule is satisfied — there is nothing to flag. No tool can determine that this spinner->check image carries the upload status (vs. decoration) and that alt="" therefore drops the busy/success information; recognizing the green check means 'submitted' requires visual + semantic reasoning.

citation.doc: WCAG Techniques ARIA22 (role=status shopping-cart example), wcag-techniques/aria/ARIA22.html
citation.quote: Because it adds visual context, the shopping cart image — with succinct and accurate alt text — is also placed in the container.

pages.scenario: Municipal CMS rich-text page editor with an autosave indicator. On Save, the aria-live="polite" indicator's DOM text is cleared and the 'Saved' state is conveyed purely by a CSS rule .saved::after { content: "\2713" } that paints a green check via generated content.
pages.mechanism: The live region's class flips to .saved and its textContent is emptied; the visible check is produced entirely by CSS ::after generated content, which is not exposed as live-region announced text in the dominant browser/AT combinations (and an empty-text class mutation gives a polite region nothing to speak). The screen-reader user who heard 'Draft'/'Saving' never hears 'Saved'. Headless check confirmed textContent == "" while computed ::after content == " ✓".
pages.selectorNote: Live region present at load (text Draft); saved state shown only via CSS glyph
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: There is no and thus no missing/empty alt for a linter to catch — the glyph is a pseudo-element. The live region is valid and pre-placed, and class-driven ::after content is an ordinary, well-formed CSS pattern that triggers no rule. Detecting the failure requires knowing CSS generated content is not reliably surfaced as live-region text AND recognizing the green check is the save status — both human/visual judgments.

citation.quote: Goal: Make users aware of important changes in content. What to do: Let assistive technology notify users about status changes that don't take focus.

pages.scenario: CI/CD pipeline dashboard (ForgeCI, payments-api). The 'Deploy to staging' stage uses a present role="status" cell; on Run deploy a spinner is injected with alt="spinner.gif" (busy) then swapped for a green check with alt="check_24.png" (done). The live region announces the asset filenames instead of the build state.
pages.mechanism: role="status" re-announces its atomic contents on change; the image's accessible name is its alt, i.e. the literal 'spinner.gif' / 'check_24.png', so the screen reader speaks the filename instead of 'application busy' / 'Deploy succeeded'. This is the present-but-misleading variant: alt is non-empty and valid but describes the file, not the status. Headless check confirmed announced text == "spinner.gif" then "check_24.png".
pages.selectorNote: Resting empty role=status; spinner img alt=filename injected on deploy
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: role="status" is present at load and every has a non-empty alt, so the 'images must have alternate text' rule passes — alt="spinner.gif" is, to a linter, simply 'alt text that exists.' No automated rule evaluates whether the alt is a useful description vs. a filename, nor whether it matches the icon's status meaning; recognizing 'spinner.gif' is a filename standing in for 'busy' requires human semantic judgment.

citation.quote: After a user activates a process, an icon symbolizing 'busy' appears on the screen. The screen reader announces "application busy".

pages.scenario: Spanish-language banking two-step verification screen (Banco Aurora, <html lang="es">). After the 6-digit code is submitted, success is shown solely by a green-check <svg role="img" aria-label="check"> injected into a present aria-live="assertive" region — a non-empty name that names the symbol's shape (and is untranslated English) rather than the verification status.
pages.mechanism: The assertive live region updates with a single role="img" SVG named 'check', so the screen reader announces the lone English word 'check' on a lang="es" page instead of 'Identidad verificada' / 'Código correcto'. The user hears a symbol name and cannot tell whether the code was accepted, rejected, or expired — present-but-misleading text alternative + language mismatch. Headless check confirmed announced text == "check" with html lang == "es".
pages.selectorNote: Resting empty aria-live; check svg labelled 'check' injected on submit
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The live region is valid and the SVG has role="img" with a non-empty aria-label, so name-presence rules pass; because 'check' plausibly matches a check-mark graphic, even a naive 'does the name describe the image' heuristic is satisfied. No tool can determine that 'check' names the symbol instead of the verification status, nor that an English label is wrong on lang="es" — both semantics and i18n require human judgment.

citation.quote: After a user submits a form, text is added to the existing form which reads, "Your form was successfully submitted." The screen reader announces the same message.

pages.scenario: PASS boundary control: a food-ordering confirmation toast (Saffron Kitchen). On Place order, a present role="alert" plays a success chime and shows a green check icon (aria-hidden), but co-locates a meaningful text node — 'Order placed — Confirmation #SK-4471 · ready ~6:45 PM' — inside the same atomic region, so the present live region announces a real status.
pages.mechanism: The role="alert" (assertive, atomic) fires on success and announces its full text content; the decorative check icon is correctly aria-hidden so it injects no stray symbol, and the chime is supplementary (its information is duplicated by the announced text). A blind user receives the same status as a sighted user — the non-text status (icon/sound) is backed by an accurate co-located text alternative. Headless check confirmed announced text == 'Order placed Confirmation #SK-4471 · ready ~6:45 PM' with icon aria-hidden == "true".
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Structurally a scanner sees the SAME shape here as in the icon-only failures — a valid live region plus an aria-hidden decorative icon — so it cannot certify this as a genuine pass on its own. Distinguishing this PASS from case-01/02 requires reading the region's text content in context and confirming it conveys the order status (and that the chime has a text/visible equivalent): the exact 'is the non-text status backed by an accurate text alternative?' judgment no rule performs.

citation.quote: Check that elements or attributes that provide information equivalent to the visual experience for the status message (such as a shopping cart image with proper alt text) also reside in the container.

aspects.title: Mis-scoping the status-message boundary: change-of-context exceptions vs. genuine in-scope status
aspects.plain: Either real status text ('No results found') is left unannounced, or trivial changes are wrongly forced into urgent announcements, because someone misjudged what truly counts as a status update.
aspects.description: This aspect tests the threshold judgment that precedes every other limb: does the dynamic change even MEET the definition of a status message (success/result, waiting, progress, or error AND not delivered via a change of context)? Two failure directions, both requiring semantic judgment: (a) FALSE POSITIVE pressure — content that the Understanding explicitly EXCEPTS is treated as needing a live region or, worse, is force-fed into role=alert and over-announces: an error shown in a focus-taking dialog (already a change of context, governed elsewhere), expand/collapse of a menu/accordion/tab (governed by 4.1.2), or new survey questions added after a response (not a status by definition); and (b) FALSE NEGATIVE pressure — a genuine status (e.g. 'No results returned', 'Your form was successfully submitted') is left out of any live region because the author wrongly decided it was 'just content' like the search results list. The distinction between 'no status message present (N/A)' and 'status message present but not programmatically determinable (fail)' is itself uncovered. Tools cannot make this call: it is about whether the message MEANS success/waiting/progress/error and whether focus moved — pure human interpretation.
aspects.scLimb: Definitional limbs A & B + scope-boundary note — F103 steps 1-2 (does-it-take-focus / does-it-convey one of the four info types); Understanding 'Examples of changes that are not status messages' + 'not to force authors to generate new status messages'.
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus has nothing distinguishing 'no status message present (N/A)' from 'status message present but not programmatically determinable (fail)', and nothing modeling the three excepted change-of-context cases. The seeds only assume a status message exists and check for a live region. Automated tools cannot determine whether a content change meets the status-message definition (success/waiting/progress/error AND no change of context) or falls under an exception — that classification is the human judgment the whole SC pivots on.

references.quote: Check that the new content provides information to the user on one of the following: the success or result of an action; the waiting state of an application; the progress of a process; the existence of errors

references.doc: Understanding 4.1.3 (Examples of changes that are not status messages)
references.quote: Since the dialog takes focus, it is defined as a change of context and does not meet the definition of a status message.

references.doc: Understanding 4.1.3 (Examples of changes that are not status messages)
references.quote: Content is exposed or hidden when a user interacts with a user interface component, for example expanding components such as a menu, select, accordion or tree... None of the resulting changes to content meet the definition of status messages.

references.doc: Understanding 4.1.3 (Other uses of live regions, note)
references.quote: The purpose of this success criterion is not to force authors to generate new status messages. Its intent is to ensure that when status messages are displayed, they are programmatically identified in a way that allows assistive technologies to present them to the user.

pages.scenario: Halcyon Credit Union wire-transfer form. On submit failure (routing number belongs to a closed institution) the page opens a real modal dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal=true) that moves focus into itself, traps Tab, and supports Esc. The error text lives entirely inside the dialog; there is deliberately no role=status/aria-live anywhere. Canonical excepted case: error delivered via a focus-taking dialog is a change of context, so it does not meet the status-message definition and 4.1.3 is N/A.
pages.mechanism: The submit handler calls focus() into the modal, so the change is announced as a dialog (change of context). Per the Understanding's 'Examples of changes that are not status messages', an error in a focus-taking dialog is excepted from 4.1.3; the absence of a live region is correct, not a defect. The only candidate message is delivered by change of context, so the SC does not apply.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Markup is fully valid (valid form, valid role=dialog+aria-modal, correct names, fine contrast) so axe/WAVE/Lighthouse report nothing — but they also cannot make the positive N/A determination. A naive 4.1.3 heuristic ('message appeared after an action but no role=status/aria-live') would FALSELY flag the dialog. Distinguishing 'no status message present (N/A)' from 'status present but not programmatically determinable (fail)' requires recognizing that focus moved into a modal — a runtime + semantic judgment no DOM linter performs.

citation.quote: An author displays an error message in a dialog. Since the dialog takes focus, it is defined as a change of context and does not meet the definition of a status message. As a result of taking focus, the new change of context is already announced by the screen reader, and thus does not need to be included in the scope of this success criterion.

pages.scenario: Cedar Mesa Pharmacy controlled-substance refill form. Submit fails the early-refill rule and the page (1) opens a role=alertdialog (aria-modal=true) and moves focus into it — a change of context that already announces the error — AND (2) also copies the same error text into a persistent role=alert aria-live=assertive banner outside the dialog. The screen-reader user hears the failure twice. Over-announcement / chattiness failure direction.
pages.mechanism: On submit, focus jumps into the alertdialog (announcing the error) while an assertive role=alert region is simultaneously populated with the same text, so AT interrupts and re-reads the message a second time regardless of cursor position; the banner persists and can re-fire on later mutation. The status mechanism is force-fed onto a message a change of context already delivered — the 'too chatty' over-announcement the Understanding warns against; the SC's purpose is not to force new status messages.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The role=alert region is exemplary ARIA — empty on load, populated after the action, assertive politeness — exactly the pattern checkers are taught to reward, so axe/WAVE/Lighthouse pass (or praise) it. No tool reasons that the SAME error is concurrently delivered by a focus-taking alertdialog, nor that two simultaneous announcements is a harm. Detecting the redundant double-surfacing requires understanding the dialog already met the goal via change of context — a contextual, AT-behavioral judgment static scans cannot make.

citation.quote: Live regions and alerts can be usefully applied in many situations where a change of content takes place which does not constitute a status message, as defined in this success criterion. However, there is a risk of making an application too "chatty" for a screen reader user. User testing should be carried out to ensure the appropriate level of feedback is achieved.

pages.scenario: Tallgrass State University LMS course-materials page with a standard APG tablist (Overview / Syllabus & policies / Readings). Selecting a tab hides one role=tabpanel and shows another — new content appears — with deliberately no role=status/aria-live. The content change is exposing/hiding content by interacting with a UI component, governed by 4.1.2, and is excepted from 4.1.3.
pages.mechanism: Tab activation toggles aria-selected, moves roving focus, and wires aria-controls/aria-labelledby, so AT announces 'Syllabus & policies, tab, selected, 2 of 3' through the widget's role/state semantics (4.1.2). Per the Understanding, selecting a different tab in a tablist does not meet the status-message definition and such state changes are already required to be exposed under 4.1.2; adding a live region would be redundant. Therefore 4.1.3 does not apply.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: Tools can verify the tab roles/attributes exist but cannot make the positive N/A call. The risk is the opposite: a heuristic that flags 'new content rendered without an aria-live region' would FALSELY fail this page. Distinguishing a 4.1.2-governed widget state change (excepted) from a genuine in-scope status lacking a live region requires knowing which SC owns the change and that tab selection is announced through role/state — a semantic boundary judgment, not a structural check.

citation.quote: Content is exposed or hidden when a user interacts with a user interface component, for example expanding components such as a menu, select, accordion or tree, or selecting a different tab item in a tablist.

pages.scenario: Riverside Folk Festival post-event satisfaction survey. Selecting a LOW overall rating ('Poor'/'Very poor') appends conditional follow-up questions (a select + free-text box) without taking focus and with no role=status/aria-live. The appended questions are new form fields, not a status message (they convey no success/waiting/progress/error), so the SC does not apply.
pages.mechanism: A change handler un-hides the follow-up block on a low rating, firing no announcement. A screen-reader user continuing through the form (next-form-field / Tab) encounters the newly-revealed, fully-labeled controls in reading order. The Understanding's third excepted example is exactly this: new survey questions added after an unhappy answer do not provide information on success/results/waiting/progress/errors, so they are not required to meet 4.1.3; announcing them is a best practice, not a requirement.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: A static scan sees valid labeled form controls with no missing attributes; a dynamic 'content appeared without an announcement' heuristic — the only automation that could touch 4.1.3 — would FALSELY flag the reveal as a missing live region. No tool can determine the appeared content is 'more questions' rather than 'a status', because that classification depends on whether the content conveys success/waiting/progress/error — the meaning-based exception that is pure human judgment.

citation.quote: After a user completes a survey question which indicates they are unhappy, a series of new questions are added to the page about customer satisfaction. The new inputs do not meet the definition of status message. They do not "provide information to the user on the success or results of an action, on the waiting state of an application, on the progress of a process or on the existence of errors," and so are not required to meet this success criterion.

pages.scenario:
Aperture Robotics careers page with a faceted job filter (Department, Location). Filtering runs client-side with no reload and without moving focus. A summary line updates to 'Showing N of 3 open roles.' or 'No roles match your filters.' rendered as a plain

with no role=status/aria-live. The results LIST is correctly not a status, but the count/empty-state summary IS a genuine status message left programmatically undeterminable. False-negative direction.
pages.mechanism:
The filter changes content without taking focus and without a page refresh (first limb met), and the summary conveys the result of an action ('No results returned' is the Understanding's own example). Because #summary is a plain

with none of output/role=status/role=alert/role=log/aria-live, AT announces nothing on the change; the user must manually hunt for the outcome. Per F103 (steps 1-4 true) a status message present but not surfaced by AT fails 4.1.3. The list — correctly not a status — sharpens that only the summary fails.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: On a static snapshot the markup is clean (labeled checkboxes, semantic <ul>, fine contrast, no missing attributes) so axe/WAVE/Lighthouse report nothing, and they never run the filter to observe the silent text swap. Even a dynamic tool would have to decide that the summary sentence (not the list) qualifies as a status requiring a live region — a meaning-based judgment about what content conveys the result of the action that tools cannot make.

citation.quote: the list of results obtained from a search are not considered a status update and thus are not covered by this success criterion. However, brief text messages displayed about the completion or status of the search, such as "Searching...", "18 results returned" or "No results returned" would be status updates if they do not take focus or cause a page refresh.

pages.scenario: Olive & Thyme restaurant reservation form. On submit the booking is confirmed without a reload and without moving focus (focus stays on the now-hidden Reserve button). Two things appear: (A) a success line 'Your table is booked…' which IS a status message, and (B) a reservation-details <dl> card (date/time/party/table) which is just booking data, like a results list, and is NOT a status. Neither is in a live region; the silent success line is the failure, the silent details card is fine. False-negative direction distinguished from a non-status list.
pages.mechanism: On submit the content changes without taking focus and without a refresh (first limb met). The success line conveys the result of an action (the Understanding's 'Your form was successfully submitted.' example). Because it lives in a plain <div> with no output/role=status/role=alert/role=log/aria-live and focus is not moved into it, AT announces nothing — the user may re-submit and double-book. Per F103 a status present but not surfaced by AT fails. The details <dl> triggers no obligation (booking data is not a status), so the failure is specifically the silent success line.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: A static scan sees a valid form, valid success <div>, and valid <dl> — all well-contrasted, no missing attributes — so axe/WAVE/Lighthouse pass, and they never submit the form to observe the silent reveal. The crux is classification: tools cannot determine that 'Your table is booked' MEANS a successful result (a status) while the adjacent details card is merely the booking data (not a status). That meaning-based discrimination, plus seeing that focus did not move, is the human interpretation the SC pivots on.

citation.quote: After a user submits a form, text is added to the existing form which reads, "Your form was successfully submitted." The screen reader announces the same message.
